name: Dirty-State Doctrine
description: Define the canonical definition of workspace dirty state. Categorize dirty sources: unsaved files in editor buffers, uncommitted changes in tracked files, unstaged files in the index, staged but uncommitted changes, untracked files, and agent-in-progress work. Each category has distinct handling rules for workspace transitions (switch, archive, close).
purpose: Without a precise dirty-state doctrine, workspaces cannot safely transition between contexts. The doctrine ensures that no work is lost during switches, archives, or shutdowns — whether that work is in editor buffers, git state, or agent-in-progress sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Dirty state is categorized: unsaved editor files, uncommitted changes, unstaged files, staged files, untracked files, agent-in-progress work
Each dirty category has a defined behavior during workspace switch (block, warn, auto-stash, auto-commit)
Each dirty category has a defined behavior during workspace archive (block, warn, auto-stash, auto-commit)
Each dirty category has a defined behavior during workspace close (block, warn, auto-save, auto-commit)
Dirty state is visible in workspace UI indicators
Agent-in-progress work has its own dirty flag, separate from git state
Combined dirty state (union of all categories) determines workspace safety for transitions
